data.name: Sharviksha
data.gender_notes: Sharviksha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess Sharva, the Goddess of prosperity and knowledge. Sharvi means 'Goddess' and Ksha means 'prosperity'. The name Sharviksha carries the meaning “Goddess of Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharviksha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Goddess Sharva is a form of Shakti, the divine mother. She is the goddess of knowledge, prosperity and strength. She is also known as Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of wisdom.
data.etymology: Sharviksha belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharviksha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sharviksha carries significant importance in Hindu culture with its reference to the Goddess Sharva. This name has evolved from belief in tradition, where names were often given based on historical or mythological figures, evoking a sense of divine blessings and protection. Sharviksha transports the bearer into a world of rich heritage, inspiring them with the ideals and values of the revered Goddess Sharva.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sharviksha also signifies the spiritual resonance of seeking prosperity, prosperity that transcends material wealth, but also encompasses the growth of wisdom, intelligence, and knowledge. Giving this name to a child is considered an auspicious act as it invokes the blessings of Goddess Sharva, who is believed to be the embodiment of knowledge, success and abundance. It is a constant reminder for the individual to uphold the virtues of wisdom and prosperity in all areas of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sharviksha: One who carries the burden of the universe with grace and compassion, embodying the divine wisdom of Shiva and the nurturing love of Lakshmi.

historical_references.reference: Sharviksha was the name of the celebrated Hindu sage who is said to have composed the 'Sharviksha Samhita' or 'Atharva Veda-Shiras-Shastra'. This text is considered as an important work in the Atharva Veda, which is one of the oldest and most revered scriptures in Hinduism. The Sharviksha Samhita is believed to have been composed around 1000 BCE.
historical_references.context: Composition of the Atharva Veda-Shiras-Shastra (Sharviksha Samhita)

historical_references.reference: Sharviksha is also mentioned in the Puranas as a powerful sage, known for his mastery over the elements and the ability to control demons. He is said to have lived during the Treta Yuga, which is the second of the four major epochs in Hindu mythology, spanning about 2 billion years ago.
historical_references.time_period: Second epoch of Hindu mythology (Treta Yuga)
